name: Kachari Ruins (Ruins of Kachari Rajbari)
description: Medieval ruins of the ancient Dimasa Kachari kingdom capital in Dimapur, featuring unique mushroom-domed sandstone pillars and carved monoliths dating to the 10th–13th centuries. Protected by the Archaeological Survey of India; remnants of temples, embankments and baths also present.
facts: Ancient capital of Dimasa Kachari kingdom before Ahom invasion
Famous for mushroom-shaped sandstone pillars up to 15 feet
Located behind Naga Shopping Arcade / near Circuit House

name: Dimapur
description: Largest city and commercial gateway of Nagaland, situated on the plains along the Dhansiri River. Main entry point by air and rail for the state; hub for markets, hotels and transit to hill districts.
facts: Largest city and main commercial centre of Nagaland
Elevation about 145 m on Dhansiri River banks
Major railway junction and airport hub
Gateway for Kohima and other hill districts

name: Nagaland Science Centre
description: Interactive science museum and educational centre in Dimapur with galleries on senses, fun science and children’s exhibits, plus a planetarium (Taramandal) and outdoor science park. Promotes scientific temper among visitors.
facts: Galleries: Our Senses, Children’s Corner, Fun Science
Located near Super Market Lane / Naga Arcade

name: NEZCC Stone Garden and North East Heritage Museum
description: North East Zone Cultural Centre complex featuring a stone sculpture garden with works by Indian artists, traditional morungs, amphitheatre and a museum showcasing crafts and artefacts from the eight northeastern states.
facts: Headquarters of North East Zone Cultural Centre
North East Heritage Museum in administrative building
Near Dimapur Airport (about 500 m–3 km from station)
Traditional morungs and amphitheatre on site

name: Green Park
description: Landscaped recreational park inside the State Horticulture Nursery at 4th Mile, Dimapur. Offers greenery, boating, picnic areas, ziplining, water zorbing and kids’ activities; popular family outing spot.
facts: Located within State Horticulture Nursery, 4th Mile
Nominal entry fee; open mainly weekends and holidays

name: Hong Kong Market
description: Bustling flea market in central Dimapur known for imported and local goods including clothing, footwear, electronics, Naga shawls and handicrafts. Vibrant commercial hub reflecting the city’s trading character.
facts: Mix of local Naga products and imported goods
Reflects city’s role as commercial gateway

name: Dimapur Ao Baptist Church
description: One of the largest Baptist churches in India, serving a large Ao Naga congregation in Dimapur. Prominent spiritual landmark reflecting the strong Christian tradition among Naga communities.
facts: Congregation of thousands of Ao families
Among the largest Baptist churches in India
Active place of worship and community

name: Dhansiri River (Dimapur Section)
description: Major river flowing along the eastern side of Dimapur, offering riverside walks, birdwatching spots and scenic sandbars. Tributary of the Brahmaputra; important natural feature of the plains gateway.
facts: Defines the plains geography of the district

name: Dimapur Jain Temple
description: Historic Jain temple built in 1947 in central Dimapur, featuring intricate glass work and ornate architecture. Important spiritual site for the local Jain community.
facts: Built in 1947 by local Jain families
Reflects multi-religious character of the city

name: Dimapur City Tower (Clock Tower)
description: Prominent landmark clock tower at Circular Road in the heart of Dimapur. Often decorated with lights during Christmas and festive seasons; a popular local meeting and photo point.
facts: Located at Circular Road in city centre
